title: China Ministry of Commerce — Cabo Verde, Cidade Segura Project Phase 3, 2026
description: "A República Popular da China disponibilizou a Cabo Verde um financiamento de cerca de 9,3 milhões de euros para a terceira fase do Projecto Cidade Segura no quadro da assistência não reembolsável acordada entre os governos dos dois países. Esse montante visa reforçar as capacidades tecnológicas e operacionais das forças de segurança e apoiar a investigação criminal." The implementation agreement was signed "esta semana" (the week of the 2026-08-15 report) by Cabo Verde's interior minister Carlos Sena and China's ambassador Zhang Yang at the National Police Command Centre in Praia. Phase 3 covers command centres, data centres and wireless base stations in Assomada, Tarrafal de Santiago and Porto Novo, plus expanded video-surveillance capacity in Praia and Mindelo. It follows Phase 1 (china-mofcom-cpv-001/china-mofcom-cpv-002) and Phase 2 (china-mofcom-cpv-003) of the same programme — neither prior tranche is held as its own record (no primary evidence found for them).

title: Japan — Cabo Verde telemedicine equipment handover, 2025
description: "Ao abrigo da Cooperação Bilateral entre o Governo de Cabo Verde, através do Ministério da Saúde e o Governo do Japão, no âmbito de um projeto denominado 'Reestruturação do Serviço Nacional de Telemedicina', o Embaixador do Japão em Dakar, AKAMATSU Takeshi, faz hoje a entrega oficial dos equipamentos de telemedicina, ao Governo de Cabo Verde." The delivery comprised 24 telemedicine units/carts, 24 videoconference systems and two digital microscopes, financed in full by the Government of Japan at CVE 240,000,000, under a project Cabo Verde had presented to Japan in 2021. Installation is under way; the Ministry states all 22 municipalities will have at least one fully telemedicine-equipped health facility, with the equipment to be integrated into the Sistema de Informação Sanitária, and the two digital microscopes installed in the two central hospitals to digitise all Anatomia Patológica slides/processes.

title: Chinese Government provides RMB 92.5 million for Phase 2 of the Safe City Project (linked to projects #56716, #88566, #88567)
description: On October 30 and 31, 2017, representatives of the Government of China and the Government of Cabo Verde signed an exchange of notes for a feasibility study on Phase 2 of the Safe City Project. According to MOFCOM, on May 16 and 20, 2019, the Chinese Government and the Government of Cabo Verde signed an exchange of notes for implementing Phase 2 of the Safe City Project. Previously, on July 10, 2017, the Cape Verde Ministry of the Interior signed an agreement with Huawei Technologies Co. on the provision of technical equipment for the project.  The Chinese Government reportedly committed RMB 92.5 million (EUR 11.8. million) in free assistance to this project. The proceeds were drawn at least in part from an Economic and Technical Cooperation Agreement (ETCA) that the two governments signed on January 31, 2018 They may have also been drawn from an agreement that the two governments signed in September 2018. This project represents the umbrella project for the funding mechanisms for the project. The January 2018 ETCA is captured in project ID#88566, and the September 2018 ETCA is captured in project ID#88567.  The purpose of Phase 2 is to extend the video surveillance network of Praia to three other Cabo Verdean islands: the island of São Vicente, especially the city of Mindelo; the island of Sal, especially the cities of Santa Maria and Espargos; and the island of Boa Vista, especially the city ​​of Sal Rei. On the island of São Vicente, 100 video surveillance poles will be installed; on the island of Sal (Ilha do Sal), 30 video surveillance poles will be installed; and on Boa Vista, 20 video surveillance poles will be installed. Phase 2 will also involve the installation of another 100 video surveillance poles in the capital city of Praia. Each of these video surveillance poles will have three cameras. title: Chinese Government provides RMB 13 million grant for Phase 2 of E-Governance Project (Linked to Project ID#55509, #52934, #55898)
description: On January 10, 2017, the Chinese Government and the Government of Cape Verde signed a preferential loan framework agreement for Phase 2 of the E-Governance Project. Then, on February 20, 2017, China Eximbank and the Government of Cape Verde signed and RMB 84.5 million government concessional loan (GCL) agreement for the same project. This loan carries the following terms: a 2% interest rate, a 20-year maturity, a 7-year grace period, 0.25% management fee, and a 0.25% commitment fee. The loan repayment period is 156 months or 13 years.   The proceeds of the loan are to be used by the borrower to fully finance an RMB 84.5 million ($13 million) commercial contract [ID#00Y1321213000C] between the Government of Cape Verde’s Núcleo Operacional da Sociedade de informação and Huawei Technologies Co., Ltd., which was signed on September 30, 2015 (captured in Project ID#52934). The Chinese Government also issued an RMB 13 million grant to the Government of Cape Verde in 2016 for Phase 2 of the E-Governance Project.   Phase 2 involved the upgrading of network infrastructure in schools, public institutions and hospitals, and the installation of computing and storage equipment to support the Government of Cape Verde’s overall e-Government (EGOV) system. title: Chinese Government provides $5 million grant for Network Access Support Project (Linked to Project ID#52933, #52934, #55509)
description: On July 11, 2016, the Chinese Ambassador to Cape Verde and Cape Verde’s Foreign Minister signed an exchange of notes for a feasibility study related to the Network Access Support Project. On January 3, 2017 and February 23, 2017, the Chinese Government and the Government of Cape Verde signed an exchange of letters for this project. The parties then signed a project implementation agreement on July 12, 2017. China’s Ministry of Commerce was the source of grant funding and it committed $5 million in total. _x000D_ _x000D_ The Network Access Support Project involved the installation of 16km of fiber optic cable, local area network (LAN) structures, WiFi networks, and equipment for public institutions that are part of the State Private Technological Network (RTPE). This project effectively provided supplemental funding for Phase 2 of the E-Governance Project (captured in Project ID#52933 and Project ID#52934). Then, on May 28, 2018, the Chinese Government and the Government of Cape Verde signed a supplementary agreement to lay an additional 1 km of fiber optic cable and extending network coverage to additional government institutions, health services, and 23 schools on Santiago Island. _x000D_ _x000D_ IT Electronic Eleventh Design Research Institute Scientific and Technological Engineering Corporation Limited (a Chinese company) and the Government of Cape Verde’s Núcleo Operacional da Sociedade de informação were responsible for project supervision. Anhui Telecommunications Engineering Co., Ltd. was the contractor responsible for project implementation. On August 10, 2018, the project officially launched and works were scheduled to end in December 2019. As of October 2019, the project was nearing completion. It was ultimately completed and handed over to the Government of Cape Verde on January 29, 2020.
